name: app-6a95e9522b4081919c5c13be9d36f908
description: Brick & Mortar answers questions about small businesses and commercial property from public records rather than general knowledge. It has sixteen tools. Five read joined public-records datasets for the seven-county Minneapolis-St. Paul metro — parcels and lot lines, recorded sale prices, tax-billing owners, rental licences, contamination files, business counts by trade, census tracts. They show what is on file for a person's role, answer one address, return true row counts, sample rows and a link to the complete file, and read a document the person brings against those records without storing it. Nine more work in any US metro and return a research procedure instead of an answer: which administrative record actually settles a question, how to reach it, and what the public record cannot answer at all. Typical workflows are tearing down one named business before buying or advising it, mapping a local competitive set, prepping broker diligence, benchmarking prices, auditing local search visibility, mining public reviews for patterns, and assembling the results into one client-ready report. Two tools send something, and only when the person asks: one sends a feature, data or correction request to the publisher, and one files an enquiry asking a person at Brick & Mortar to read the record for them; that person replies by email. Those two are the only tools that are not read-only. No account is needed.

defaultPrompt: What Twin Cities property records can you pull?
What commercial property sold near 2900 Hennepin Ave, Minneapolis?
Where do I find restaurant health inspections in Denver?

positive.description: List the public-records datasets available for the Twin Cities, with real row counts.
positive.prompt: What Twin Cities datasets do you have?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns every published dataset (39 on 2026-10-09) with its title, true row count, column names and the counties it covers.

positive.description: Answer a property question from the joined recorded-sales records.
positive.prompt: What commercial property sold within half a mile of 2900 Hennepin Ave, Minneapolis?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the true matching row count, up to six example rows with sale price and date, and a link to the complete file.

positive.description: Tear down one named small business before advising or buying it.
positive.prompt: Tear down Kramarczuk's Sausage Company in Minneapolis.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the four-quadrant teardown framework — presence, perception, position and performance — with a research procedure and quality rubric.

positive.description: Locate the administrative record that settles a question in a metro outside the Twin Cities.
positive.prompt: Where do I find restaurant health inspections in Denver?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a source-first research plan naming the specific public record, how to reach it, and what it cannot answer.

positive.description: Build a defensible local price comparison in a category where competitors publish little.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a normalisation framework for comparing differing service bundles, including what to do when prices are not published.

negative.description: Do not trigger for requests to modify a public record; the app is read-only.
negative.prompt: Delete the parcel record for 123 Main St.

negative.description: Do not return records for an address outside the seven-county Minneapolis-St. Paul metro.
negative.prompt: What did 1600 Pennsylvania Ave in Washington, DC sell for?

negative.description: Do not trigger for a request to contact a third party; the two tools that send anything write only to the publisher, never to an owner.
negative.prompt: Email that property's owner and ask whether they would sell.

review.commerce_description: No purchase or payment happens in ChatGPT. One tool files an enquiry with a person at Brick & Mortar, who replies by email.

publication.release_notes: 1.1.1: moves the listing to the plugin package format. The description now covers all 16 tools the server serves; four tools added since the last scan (what_we_have_for_you, twin_cities_lookup, bring_your_document, start_an_engagement) carry explicit true/false annotations like every other tool. Skills updated to match.
